gold_rationale: A brain-penetrant, selective LRRK2 kinase inhibitor is mechanistically well-aligned with LRRK2 gain-of-function PD (elevated kinase activity -> endolysosomal dysfunction), with a tractable target-engagement biomarker (pRab10). Progression should be conditional on demonstrating the CNS exposure and selectivity, clearing standard ADMET/safety liabilities, and — the key gating issue — defining a peripheral on-target safety window: LRRK2 inhibition causes lung (type II pneumocyte / surfactant) and kidney changes, so partial inhibition, reversibility, and pulmonary/renal monitoring are required. Patient stratification toward LRRK2-variant carriers strengthens the case. Mechanistic plausibility is not proven disease modification.
required_concepts: peripheral on-target safety (lung type II pneumocyte / kidney)
red_flags: claims proven disease modification without sufficient clinical evidence
ignores peripheral on-target LRRK2 safety (lung / kidney)
ignores kinase selectivity or standard ADMET/safety liabilities
treats potency/selectivity as sufficient without a safety window
